notes.etonnya: Cwer is to fall, for rain.
notes.eggulu: Polo is the sky; thunder is polo mor, the sky roaring.
notes.ekyeya: Oro, the dry season, roughly November to March.

guidebook.intro: Acholi land has two seasons: **cwir**, the rains, and **oro**, the hot dry season.

tips.title: Kot tye ka cwer
body: Rain falls: **Kot tye ka cwer** (it’s raining). The sun shines: **Ceng ryeny**. **Polo**, the sky, roars when it thunders: **Polo tye ka mor**.
**Awinyo** (I feel, I hear) tells how you feel: **Awinyo koyo** (I feel cold), **Awinyo lyeto** (I feel hot).

tips.title: Cwir and oro
body: **Cwir** runs from about April to October, the time of planting. **Oro** is from about November to March, when the grass dries and the wind blows dust.

culture.title: Rain is welcome
body: When the first rains come, everyone goes to the fields. A storm that keeps you at a friend’s house is a good reason for tea and stories.
